title: from method reachability to parameter reachability
segments: 6-1 task orchestration: multi-line goal, acceptance criteria, dependencies and the coding switch from a terminal editor
6-2 session management: a session picker, a shared reload path for switching and creation, and per-session requirement visibility
6-3 task detail and result enhancement: a task/get detail view, blocked-reason recall, and diff-only colouring of the file-diff attachment
6-4 real API and Keychain verification: a real probe and coding task, a recorded approval path, and a loopback failure matrix
status: 6-1 through 6-4 complete, including a real-provider run and the failure matrix; 6-5 packaging is out of scope
scope: stage 5 made all 19 host methods reachable, but the client always sent empty task parameters, could only bind a session at startup, showed task metadata only in fragments, and had never been verified against a real provider. 6-1 makes the task parameters reachable, 6-2 makes every persisted session switchable, 6-3 makes a task's full host snapshot readable in one place, 6-4 proves the whole chain against a real OpenAI-compatible endpoint

contract_coverage.note: no new method in 6-1/6-2: `task/create` now carries its full parameter set instead of constants, and `session/list` gained a picker instead of being a startup-only call

task_editor.key_correction: Ctrl+I was the original plan but a terminal delivers it as 0x09, the same byte as Tab, so it can never be a distinct binding; Ctrl+F keeps the Ctrl+letter convention used by the other modals
task_editor.fields: 0 goal, 1 acceptance, 2 dependencies, 3 coding; Tab/BackTab cycle, Esc cancels
task_editor.multiline: Enter inserts a newline in the goal and acceptance fields (goal <= 64000 bytes, acceptance <= 16000 bytes); Space is plain text there. Enter on a pane without the editor still dispatches immediately with empty acceptance and no dependencies, byte-for-byte as before
task_editor.acceptance_required: the editor rejects an empty acceptance and keeps the form open, pointing at the Enter quick-dispatch path; the host itself still allows empty acceptance
task_editor.dependencies: candidates come from the current session's task/list; at most 8 (MAX_DEPENDENCIES); failed/cancelled/interrupted/blocked tasks cannot be selected and say so (`勾选后新任务会直接阻塞`); a completed coding task that is not integrated is labelled 等待集成; the window shows 8 rows and scrolls with the cursor
task_editor.coding: the switch starts from the pane's current coding toggle and is sent as `coding` in the same request
task_editor.caret: text fields share TextBuf { text, cursor } with the pane input line, so caret arithmetic exists once; the editor marks the focused field with an inline `❙` instead of moving the terminal cursor, which keeps wrapped lines correct, and a stale cursor is clamped to a char boundary before rendering

dispatch.helper: client.rs::dispatch_task is the single shape for both paths: Action::Send (legacy quick dispatch) and Action::CreateTask (editor) build the same task/create request
dispatch.validation: goal non-empty and within the limit; acceptance non-empty and within the limit; dependency ids are a subset of the rendered candidates; the host stays authoritative and its errors are echoed verbatim with the form still open
dispatch.blocked_events: the client handles task_blocked and appends `[依赖] 任务已阻塞：<host reason>` to the pane in the warning colour

session_picker.scope: live mode only; demo mode keeps the key inert and the pty probe asserts it
session_picker.rows: short id, validation-command count and a current marker; the picker keeps an 8-row window around the highlight and shows the total when there are more sessions
session_picker.detail: repository, branch, base commit and the user-constraint summary of the highlighted session; missing fields render as `—`, and long paths are clipped on a char boundary
session_picker.requirements: opening the picker reads event/list (after=0, limit=1000) once per session and keeps the newest 3 requirement/user_override records; results are cached per session, and publishing a new constraint invalidates only the current session's cache. Empty records are ignored
session_picker.keys: Up/Down move, Enter switches (or closes with a note when it is already the current session), Ctrl+R re-reads, Esc closes

session_switch.path: Action::SwitchSession, startup auto-attach and Ctrl+N creation all call Client::attach, so no entry point can skip a reset step
session_switch.reset: attach drops the pending-request map (late answers from the old session become inert and cannot reopen an old task/output view), clears after/task maps/artifacts/probe/output poll, and calls App::reset_session_view, which replaces the panes with empty placeholders and clears shared records, approvals and every per-session modal
session_switch.kept: focus, zoom, shared-panel visibility and the coding toggle are global user choices and survive a switch
session_switch.reload: attach then runs agent/list -> task/list + event/list(after=0) + approval/list, the same catch-up path used everywhere else
session_switch.empty_requirement_fix: Ctrl+N used to send `requirement: ""`; the host records whatever it receives, so every new session gained a blank user constraint. The client now omits the field when it is empty (`create_session_params`)

footer: hints moved to two lines: the global line carries Ctrl+A/Ctrl+L/Ctrl+K and the task line carries Ctrl+T/Ctrl+U/Ctrl+O/Ctrl+D/Ctrl+F/Ctrl+E/Ctrl+G/Ctrl+P/Ctrl+N; a 132-column render test asserts every hint is unabridged

suite.ignored_reason: core runtime_e2e needs installed Codex; tui real-host smoke needs a built codex-collab-core
suite.regressions_guarded: the existing panes/input/history tests were kept and only adapted to TextBuf, so Enter dispatch, paste, history and caret editing stay covered; the picker's Ctrl+L is added to the footer regression list

opt_in.real_host_smoke: passed: the ignored test still drives a real codex-collab-core process through session/create, agent/configure, agent/list, task/list, approval/list, task/get, task/integrate, context/compact, agent/testConnection, agent/connectionResult, event/publish and task/output

pty_demo_smoke: passed: four panes, the live-only Ctrl+F and Ctrl+L stay inert in demo mode and do not steal focus, paste/send, caret editing, stop, confirmed quit, terminal restoration, non-TTY rejection
pty_live_smoke: passed: after seeding a session and agent, Ctrl+F opened the task editor, Enter inserted a newline rather than dispatching, Tab reached acceptance and the dependency list, space toggled the coding field, and Ctrl+S queued the task; Ctrl+D then opened task/get and showed the submitted acceptance plus the task/get-only context version. Then Ctrl+U published a requirement, Ctrl+N created a second session on the same repository (panes showed 未配置 and the shared panel had no records), Ctrl+L listed `共 2 个会话` with the current marker, Up + Enter switched back, and the seeded model plus both user records reappeared. After the TUI exited, the host confirmed two sessions with disjoint agents, tasks and user events, and the requirement still in the first session's log
pty_render_note: ratatui emits only changed cells and the inline caret changes one cell per keystroke, so the live probe strips escape sequences and the `❙` marker before matching contiguous text, and drains until an expected needle appears instead of sleeping a fixed time
screen_snapshot: evidence/stage-6-task-screen.txt is a live 40x132 frame of the task editor; evidence/stage-6-detail-screen.txt is a live 34x132 task/get round-trip showing the failed probe task with `—` for workspace/base/commit and the host's result text; evidence/stage-6-sessions-screen.txt is a live 30x132 frame of the picker over three real sessions on one repository; evidence/stage-6-real-detail-screen.txt and evidence/stage-6-real-output-screen.txt are live 34x132 frames of the real task's task/get detail (integrated) and its output view (file-diff preview)

real_api.endpoint: https://<provider>/v1 (redacted per the stage 6 boundary; the concrete value stays in the operator's state directory and Keychain)
real_api.protocol: chat_completions through the Responses->Chat conversion (cross-protocol requests drop reasoning)
real_api.credential: written by the operator through Ctrl+K into Keychain service dev.codex.collab; the scripts never read, print or store the key
real_api.probe: agent/testConnection -> agent/connectionResult: verified=true, capabilities text/stream/function_tools, result connection_probe_ok
real_api.coding_task: completed; the model wrote hello.txt, the host committed 9d9b1ce and published a 133-byte file-diff attachment; task/integrate re-ran the validation in the integration worktree and moved head e63ada7 -> aee0946
real_api.approvals: two item/commandExecution/requestApproval calls (the model's own git commit and git config, blocked because the worktree .git lives outside the sandbox root); the replay harness --approve prints and records each command and reason before accepting, and without --approve it stops with an explicit waiting-for-approval error instead of timing out
real_api.failure_matrix: scripts/stage6_errors.py covers the address rule (non-loopback http, query and credentials rejected; https and loopback accepted), a Keychain set/delete round-trip on a throwaway agent id, upstream 401 (1 request, no retry), 429 (3 requests then give up), transport failure (502, not replayed) and a missing credential (Keychain credential unavailable)
real_api.code_change: turn/completed used to drop turn.error.message, so every upstream failure read `Agent turn failed or interrupted`; the message is now redacted and surfaced, with a fixture test
real_api.limits: chat_completions was exercised against the provider; responses has only unit and mock-upstream coverage. 401/429/transport were exercised against a loopback fake upstream, not the provider. The model's own summary claims the commit failed, which contradicts the committed candidate hash and the diff attachment

evidence_script: scripts/stage6_evidence.sh replays build -> workspace tests -> opt-in tests -> clippy -> fmt -> both pty probes -> both snapshots and rewrites evidence/stage-6-tests.log; scripts/stage6_real_evidence.sh replays the real run (needs STATE and SESSION, spends money) and scripts/stage6_errors.py runs the loopback failure matrix offline
log: evidence/stage-6-tests.log (default suite), evidence/stage-6-real.log (real run plus both live snapshots)

task_detail.scope: live mode only, focused pane's latest task; PgUp/PgDn scroll, Ctrl+R re-reads the snapshot, Esc closes
task_detail.source: task/get; the view is a read-only host snapshot and every field maps one to one
task_detail.fields: status, coding, contextVersion, worktree, baseCommit, commit, integrationStatus (未集成/已集成/存在冲突/集成失败/集成中断), goal, acceptance, dependencies as short id plus the status from the last task/list, block reason, result summary, attachment inventory and the full-result attachment
task_detail.missing_values: an unset field renders `—` or `（空）`; the view never infers a worktree, commit or integration state
task_detail.blocked_reason: the host only reports a block reason in the task_blocked event, so the client keeps the latest reason per task id (cleared on session switch) and shows it verbatim; without the event the line is absent
task_detail.attachments: artifacts and the full result come from the same local read_attachment helper as task/output, with no new path source and no user-supplied paths

result_modal.diff_preview: the output view now also reads the file-diff attachment (same helper and byte cap) and colours it line by line
result_modal.highlighting: `@@` hunk headers in the accent colour, `+++`/`---` file headers muted, `+` additions green, `-` deletions in the warning colour, everything else plain; no syntax parsing and no width assumptions
result_modal.shared_code: the review modal uses the same push_diff helper, still truncating at 300 lines with the total noted
result_modal.boundaries: empty text, a missing trailing newline, CJK, and a 10k-character single line are pushed unchanged and left to the renderer's wrapping; a non-UTF-8 attachment already fails at the read step and never reaches the highlighter
